task: Add replay protection to the Paystack webhook handler so a captured event can't be re-submitted.
project_summary: A payments service that receives Paystack webhooks (charge.success, transfer events) and updates order state. The handler already verifies the HMAC signature, but it does not defend against replayed or duplicated deliveries.
current_direction: Harden the existing verified handler against replay and duplicate delivery before enabling automatic order fulfilment.

decisions.title: Reject events whose timestamp is outside a 5-minute window
decisions.body: Parse the delivery timestamp and reject anything older than 5 minutes (or in the future), after the signature check passes.
decisions.rationale: A leaked-but-valid payload should not be replayable indefinitely; a bounded window limits the blast radius.
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires reasonably synced clocks; we allow 5 minutes of skew rather than a tighter window to avoid false rejections.

evidence.claim: Paystack signs each event with HMAC SHA512 using your secret key; verify before trusting the body

decisions.title: Deduplicate on the event id with a persisted seen-set
decisions.body: Record each processed event id and treat a repeat id as already-handled (return 200 without re-processing).
decisions.rationale: Signature + timestamp still allow the SAME event to be delivered twice within the window; idempotency must key on the event id.
decisions.tradeoffs: Adds a small store and a TTL to prune old ids; acceptable for correctness.

sources.label: Paystack — Verifying webhooks
sources.bound_claim: Paystack signs each event with HMAC SHA512 using your secret key; verify before trusting the body

constraints: The HMAC signature check must run first and stay unchanged — do not weaken it.
Always respond within Paystack's timeout; return 200 for already-seen events so they stop retrying.
Never log the raw signature, secret key, or full request body.
boundaries: Only touch the webhook ingestion path; do not change order-fulfilment business logic.
No new third-party dependency without a stated reason.
what_to_avoid: Trusting the event body before the signature is verified.
Keying idempotency on the reference alone — use the delivered event id.
open_questions: Which persistent store holds the seen-set — the existing Postgres, or Redis with a TTL?
What clock-skew window is acceptable to operations?
next_steps: Add timestamp-window rejection after the existing signature check.
Add event-id dedupe backed by a persisted seen-set with a TTL.
Add tests: valid new event, replayed event, expired timestamp, tampered signature.
definition_of_done: A replayed or duplicated delivery is safely ignored (200, no double-processing), an out-of-window event is rejected, the signature check is unchanged, and tests cover the four cases.

recommended_assistant.reason: This is a bounded implementation task in an existing repo with clear tests to write.
